literal: Not desiring the things that kings desire will give enduring wealth by those kings.
translation: Abstaining from desiring the very things that rulers desire for themselves will bring enduring prosperity through those same rulers.
modern: அரசர்கள் விரும்பும் பொருள்களைத் தான் விரும்பாமல் இருப்பது, அந்த அரசர்களாலேயே ஒருவருக்கு நிலைத்த செல்வத்தைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet advises courtiers and associates on how to behave safely and successfully around rulers. The word 'viḻaipa' refers to the specific objects, pleasures, or privileges that a king desires or enjoys. By practicing 'viḻaiyāmai' (not desiring those same things), an associate avoids provoking the ruler's jealousy, suspicion, or rivalry. This self-restraint wins the ruler's trust, which ultimately yields 'manniya ākkam' (enduring wealth and position) bestowed by the ruler himself.
